result.rationale: The diff's new members action sets `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` with no maximum and applies it to all groups, whereas the old code only applied a capped-by-caller limit (default 200) to automatic groups; an attacker can now pass limit=1000000 on any visible group and force serialization of every user. The mechanism is verifiable in the diff and is a real security/resource-exhaustion regression.

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff changes pagination to always use `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and applies it directly in `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)` with no upper bound. That makes `?limit=1000000` (or similar) request-controlled and can force the server to load/serialize an extremely large member list (plus it also does an unconditional `group.users.count`). This is a concrete, diff-visible resource-exhaustion risk.
